The Section 5 application uses processed microbiome abundance tables derived from `curatedMetagenomicData`, generated comparison samples, and saved log-density-ratio outputs from the prior submission. ### Additional Information (optional)

The original public source for the application is `curatedMetagenomicData` (Pasolli et al., *Nature Methods* 14, 1023–1024, 2017; doi:10.1038/nmeth.4468). The supplied processed CSV files document the starting point of the prior submitted application workflow. Full upstream acquisition and preprocessing, the final Round 2 application figure lineage, and permission to redistribute each processed or generated file remain subject to Section 5 coauthor confirmation. The technical 50-repeat studies are represented by saved seed-level results, selected detailed RDS files, source code, and provenance records. The complete transformed 20D BART RDS set is approximately 14 GB and is not included; its seed-level summaries and recomputation code are included.

# Part 2: Code

## Abstract

The archive contains the BATTS source revision used by the Round 2 simulations, the prior submitted method and comparator source, scripts for simulation, summarization, and figure rendering, and release-specific commands for drawing and light runs. Saved seed-level results permit regeneration of the technical tables and most figures without rerunning all 50 seeds. The Section 5 code and inputs are included as prior-submission reference material pending final coauthor confirmation.

### Supporting software requirements

#### Version of primary software used

The original and local Round 2 checks used R 4.5.2. The portable table command uses Python 3; **[AUTHOR TO RECORD the tested Python version before submission]**. A compatible C++ compiler toolchain is needed to install the bundled R source packages. The Section 5 Python environment and its final code path require coauthor confirmation.

#### Libraries and dependencies used by the code

`code/BATTS/` is the BATTS source at Git commit `6f625bad83702b36e5480be1ed1343258a9b075a`. The Round 2 workflow source is identified as commit `f921525711faef2a326c561820749e0c70f1bf42`. Prior source copies of `ReviewPkg` 0.0.0.9000 and the corrected `densratio` 0.2.1 are in `reference/r1/code/methods/`. Local drawing checks used `ggplot2` 4.0.3, `patchwork` 1.3.2, `scales` 1.4.0, `mvtnorm` 1.3.3, and `pracma` 2.4.6. The completed light checks used `ReviewPkg` 0.0.0.9000, `densratio` 0.2.1, `mvtnorm` 1.3.6, and `ada` 2.0.5.1; the 20D path also uses `pracma`. Further dependencies for canonical recomputation are identified in `code/r2/scripts/` and `ENVIRONMENT.md`. **[AUTHOR TO ADD the clean-environment dependency record and final package versions.]**

# Part 3: Reproducibility workflow

## Scope

The provided workflow reproduces:

- [ ] Any numbers provided in text in the paper
- [x] The computational method(s) presented in the paper (i.e., code is provided that implements the method(s))
- [ ] All tables and figures in the paper
- [x] Selected tables and figures in the paper, as explained and justified below:

The supplied saved inputs and commands regenerate Main Tables 1–2, the transformed 20D and CDC supplementary tables, and the technical main and supplementary figures described in `FIGURE_TABLE_MAP.md`. All 264 displayed numerical table entries were checked against the final local TeX after rounding to three decimals. Fourteen regenerated technical PDFs matched the corresponding local manuscript assets pixel for pixel at 110 dpi. Main Figure 2 can be regenerated at its fixed seed, although its current panel geometry differs from the manuscript PDF. Section 5 final figures remain pending coauthor confirmation of their Round 2 data and code lineage. The source scripts allow full 50-seed recomputation, while the archive retains seed-level summaries and selected detailed RDS files for practical review. The light run uses the displayed data seed with reduced computational settings; its estimates can differ from the paper and are labeled `SMOKE_NOT_FOR_PAPER`.

### Instructions

Unzip the archive and work from `reproducibility_materials_review/`. Read `README.md` for the directory layout, exact commands, and the requirement to write into a new output directory outside the supplied `reference/` and `results/` trees. `FIGURE_TABLE_MAP.md` identifies each technical table and figure, its saved inputs, code, and verification status. `ENVIRONMENT.md` documents source revisions and locally tested dependencies; `VALIDATION_STATUS.md` records completed checks and unresolved items. Verify the package inventory with `python code/verify_bundle.py`.

For the four technical tables, run `python code/portable/reproduce_tables.py <new-output-dir>`. The README gives individual drawing commands for the main and supplementary figures; each command takes saved results and writes to a separate new output directory. To exercise a simulation computation at the displayed 2D Figure 3 seed, use `Rscript code/light/run_light.R --family=2d --scenario=local_shift --n0=5000 --n1=5000 --seed=1 --lib-dir=<installed-R-library> --output-dir=<new-output-dir>`. For the 20D supplementary location surface, use the same entry point with `--family=20d --scenario=latent_location_shift --n0=5000 --n1=5000 --seed=21`. The 2D supplementary surface settings and data seeds are listed in `FIGURE_TABLE_MAP.md`. These reduced runs are workflow checks; the archived seed-level results are used for the reported 50-repeat summaries.
